title: Save reference drum rack presets and clips from the DAW into a fixture folder
description:
## Intent

Get ground truth: reference files saved by the DAW itself, so every later spec compares Apricity's output with what the DAW writes, not with guesses.

## Steps (the owner does the DAW part; an agent annotates)

1. In the DAW, build a drum rack with four pads, each a sampler holding a short WAV from the library:
   - pad 1 untouched (C1);
   - pad 2 with root key moved, transpose +3 st and detune -20 cents;
   - pad 3 with sample start/end narrowed and volume -6 dB;
   - pad 4 warped (warp on, two warp markers moved), playback in classic mode with a short release.
2. Save it as a preset: `kit-reference.adg`. Save a second copy after changing only pad 2's receiving note (to isolate the note encoding).
3. Save two clips: `clip-warped.alc` (a loop, named, with an info text) and `clip-unwarped.alc` (warp off).
4. Copy the files into `crates/apricity-daw/tests/fixtures/reference/` with a `README.md` listing what each one holds and the DAW version that wrote it. No audio: the files only reference audio paths.

## Out of scope

Writing any product code; the `.alc` anatomy in depth (sidecar initiative apricitus-d7746d).

## Verification

```sh
for f in crates/apricity-daw/tests/fixtures/reference/*.{adg,alc}; do gzip -t "$f" && gunzip -c "$f" | xmllint --noout - ; done
git check-ignore -q crates/apricity-daw/tests/fixtures/reference/*.wav && echo "no audio tracked"
```

Manual: the owner reopens each file in the DAW and it loads as saved.

## Release

`chore(<this task id>): reference presets and clips saved by the DAW`. Not breaking.

## Log

Record in comments: the DAW version, anything the DAW changed on save, any file that would not load.
